subject.title: RFC: Standard Hosting Profiles and Ready Check

question: Should OpenClaw core own named hosting profiles as release-tested readiness contracts, or expose only generic runtime facts for hosts and policy tooling to compose?
rationale: The RFC is technically coherent, but current main already has an adjacent configuration-conformance boundary; choosing which layer permanently owns topology contracts requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Stage the core foundation
options.body: Accept the canonical condition/result model first and require separate compatibility approval for each named profile and authoritative predicate.

options.title: Accept the full profile catalog
options.body: Adopt all four profiles, precedence rules, readiness failures, and the release matrix as one core support contract.

options.title: Keep profile composition external
options.body: Expose stable runtime facts from core while hosts or policy tooling define named topology-specific readiness contracts.

recommendation.title: Stage the core foundation
recommendation.body: Accept the canonical condition/result model first and require separate compatibility approval for each named profile and authoritative predicate.

likelyOwner.reason: Their history most directly owns the RFC acceptance lifecycle and accepted-contract structure needed to route this decision.
